advances: This concerns an auxiliary ordinary fixed-cap circuit. The mark need not be deepest, the individual sections need not be centroidal there, and the caps need not have equal volume.

proof:
Write $F_j=\{\lambda_j=0\}\cap K$ and let $v_i$ be vertex $i$. The section $\{\lambda_i=a_i\}\cap K$ is $a_i v_i+t_i F_i$, so its area is $S_i=A_i t_i^{d-1}$. The normal $u_i$ pointing toward higher $\lambda_i$ is the negative of the outward normal of $F_i$. The divergence theorem for constant fields gives $\sum_i A_i u_i=0$. Thus $\theta_i S_i=A_i/Z$ gives the desired balance.

On $F_j$, the cap $H_i$ is empty if $i=j$. Otherwise $F_j\cap H_i=a_i v_i+t_i F_j$, since $v_i\in F_j$ and the barycentric-coordinate inequality is the usual vertex cap. Therefore for each $j$,
$$
\sum_i\theta_i |F_j\cap H_i|_{d-1}
  =\sum_{i\ne j}(t_i^{1-d}/Z)t_i^{d-1}A_j=(d/Z)A_j.
$$

For the signed variation, let $R>\max_{x\in L}|x|$ and denote the unit outward normal of $F_j$ by $n_j$. The symmetric difference of $K+\tau L$ and $K$ lies within $R\tau$ of $\partial K$. The exterior assertion follows from $K+\tau L\subseteq K+R\tau\mathbb B_d$. For the interior assertion choose any $l\in L$ and use $K+\tau l\subseteq K+\tau L$. Points with distance greater than $R\tau$ from the boundary remain in $K+\tau l$. Along normal lines over $F_j$ at tangential distance greater than $C\tau$ from its relative boundary, for a sufficiently large fixed $C$, the upper boundary in this strip is exactly at signed height $\tau h_L(n_j)$. Indeed the support inequality is necessary. For sufficiency choose $l_j\in L$ with $n_j\cdot l_j=h_L(n_j)$ and subtract $\tau l_j$ from a point at that height or below it in the strip. The facet-$j$ inequality then holds. Each other facet inequality still holds because its slack on the tangentially trimmed facet is bounded below by its tangent-gradient norm times the trim width, or by a positive constant for a parallel facet. The displacement is at most $2R\tau$, and finitely many inequalities allow one common $C$. Thus the entire relevant strip below that height lies in $K+\tau L$.

The parts of the symmetric difference omitted by this description are within $O(\tau)$ of the union of faces of dimension at most $d-2$ and have volume $O(\tau^2)$. This follows by taking a nearest boundary point and, if it is far from the relative boundary of a facet, using the normal line to that facet. The omitted pieces are then covered by finitely many tubes of radius $O(\tau)$ around bounded faces of codimension at least two. For any $H_i$, restricting to the cap keeps exactly the strips over $F_j\cap H_i$ up to another $O(\tau^2)$ error. If its cutting hyperplane meets $F_j$ transversely in the facet plane, the ambiguous footprint lies in a width-$O(\tau)$ slab in that plane. If the hyperplane is parallel to that plane, it has positive separation because the cap is proper and the facet is supporting. In the first case the slab area is $O(\tau)$ and the strip height is $O(\tau)$. This gives the right derivatives
$$
D|K+\tau L|=\sum_j A_j h_L(n_j),\qquad
D|(K+\tau L)\cap H_i|=\sum_j |F_j\cap H_i|_{d-1}h_L(n_j).
$$
The weighted facet trace identity now gives the asserted equality for all summands.

If $0\in L$ the direction is outward. For a positive total derivative the ratio is $d/Z$. Strict convexity of $x^{1-d}$ on $x>0$ and $\sum_i t_i=d$ give $Z\ge(d+1)(d/(d+1))^{1-d}$ with equality exactly at equal $t_i$. If some $a_i\to1$, then $t_i\to0$ and $Z\to\infty$. For $(a_0,a_1,a_2)=(1/2,1/4,1/4)$, the weights are $(3/7,2/7,2/7)$, so $d/Z=3/7=4/9-1/63$.

statement:
Let $K$ be a $d$-simplex, $d\ge2$, and $x_0$ an interior point with barycentric coordinates $a_i=\lambda_i(x_0)$. Put $t_i=1-a_i$, and fix the caps $H_i=\{\lambda_i\ge a_i\}$ through $x_0$, with unit normals $u_i$ pointing into them. Let $A_i$ be the area of facet $\lambda_i=0$, $S_i=A_i t_i^{d-1}$ the cap section measure, $Z=\sum_i t_i^{1-d}$, and $\theta_i=t_i^{1-d}/Z$. Then $\sum_i\theta_i S_i u_i=0$. For every nonempty compact convex Minkowski summand $L$, the right derivatives at $\tau=0$ satisfy
$$
\sum_i\theta_i\frac{d}{d\tau}\big|(K+\tau L)\cap H_i\big|
=\frac dZ\frac{d}{d\tau}|K+\tau L|.
$$
For outward directions with positive total derivative, this ratio is $d/Z\le\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, with equality exactly at the centroid. It tends to zero as one $a_i$ tends to one. For the planar barycentrics $(1/2,1/4,1/4)$, the weights are $(3/7,2/7,2/7)$ and the ratio is $3/7=4/9-1/63$.
title: A section-balanced simplex circuit can have an arbitrarily small Minkowski derivative ratio
